questions.question: Which HTTP methods should I use to send a request body?

expected.evidence: POST (the most common), PUT, DELETE or PATCH

questions.question: Can I send a body in a GET request with FastAPI?

expected.evidence: supported by FastAPI, only for very complex/extreme use cases

questions.question: How do I make a field of my Pydantic model optional?

expected.evidence: Use None to make it just optional.

questions.question: What happens when the data sent by the client is invalid?

expected.evidence: return a nice and clear error, indicating exactly where and what was the incorrect data

questions.question: How does FastAPI decide if a parameter is path, query or body?

evidence: it will be used as a path parameter
singular type (like int, float, str, bool, etc) it will be interpreted as a query parameter
it will be interpreted as a request body

questions.question: Does writing `str | None` make a query parameter optional?

expected.evidence: it will know it's not required because it has a default value of = None

questions.question: Do I have to use Pydantic to receive body data?

expected.evidence: you can also use Body parameters
you can instruct FastAPI to treat it as another body key using Body

questions.question: Can I reuse the JSON Schema generated for my models elsewhere?

expected.evidence: you can also use them anywhere else you like

questions.question: Is there a plugin that improves Pydantic support in PyCharm?

expected.evidence: Pydantic PyCharm Plugin

questions.question: Why is my request body not showing up in the Swagger UI docs for a specific endpoint?

expected.evidence: won't show the documentation for the body when using GET

questions.question: How do I read the actual values sent in the JSON payload from inside my route function?

expected.evidence: Inside of the function, you can access all the attributes of the model object directly

questions.question: Why is it discouraged to send a body in a GET request?

expected.evidence: has an undefined behavior in the specifications

questions.question: How are query parameters sent in a request?

expected.evidence: The query is the set of key-value pairs that go after the ? in a URL, separated by & characters.

questions.question: How can I deserialize a response?

expected.evidence: Read the body of the request as JSON
Serialize the returned data to JSON using Pydantic

questions.question: Why does /users/me return the wrong result when /users/{user_id} is declared first?

expected.evidence: Because *path operations* are evaluated in order

questions.question: How do I make a path parameter contain a full path, like home/johndoe/myfile.txt?

expected.evidence: /files/{file_path:path}

questions.question: Does OpenAPI support path parameters that contain a path?

expected.evidence: OpenAPI doesn't support a way to declare a *path parameter* to contain a *path* inside

questions.question: Why do I receive item_id as an int and not as the string from the URL?

evidence: <dfn title="converting the string that comes from an HTTP request into Python data">"parsing"</dfn>

questions.question: Does declaring q as `str | None` without a default make a Query parameter optional?

expected.evidence: does not make a query parameter optional

questions.question: How do I make a query parameter required when I use Query?

evidence: you can simply not declare a default value

questions.question: How can I use a query parameter name that is not a valid Python variable, like item-query?

expected.evidence: you can declare an `alias`

questions.question: How do I hide a query parameter from the generated OpenAPI docs?

expected.evidence: include_in_schema

questions.question: Why is my extra `importance` field treated as a query parameter instead of part of the JSON body?

expected.evidence: because it is a singular value, **FastAPI** will assume that it is a query parameter

questions.question: How do I make FastAPI expect a JSON with an `item` key when I only have one body model?

expected.evidence: Body(embed=True)

questions.question: How do I receive several Pydantic models in the same request body?

expected.evidence: Multiple body parameters

questions.question: How do I avoid returning the user's plaintext password in the response?

expected.evidence: FastAPI** will take care of filtering out all the data that is not declared in the output model

questions.question: Can I annotate the return type with a parent class and still filter fields from the response?

expected.evidence: make sure that what you return includes **only** the fields that are declared in the type

questions.question: Why do editors and mypy not complain when I return UserIn from a function annotated as BaseUser?

expected.evidence: `UserIn` is a subclass of `BaseUser`

questions.question: How do I override the default response for invalid request data?

expected.evidence: @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)

questions.question: Why shouldn't I return str(exc) of a RequestValidationError directly?

expected.evidence: you could be leaking a bit of information about your system

questions.question: Should I register my handler for FastAPI's HTTPException or Starlette's?

expected.evidence: you should register it for Starlette's `HTTPException`

questions.question: Do I return or raise an HTTPException?

expected.evidence: you don't `return` it, you `raise` it

questions.question: How should I write the CMD in my Dockerfile so FastAPI shuts down gracefully?

expected.evidence: Make sure to always use the exec form to ensure that FastAPI can shutdown gracefully

questions.question: Should I use --workers inside each container when my cluster already replicates containers?

expected.evidence: you would not want to have multiple workers in the container

questions.question: Why is running a single process per container good for memory management?

expected.evidence: you will have a more or less well-defined, stable, and limited amount of memory consumed by each of those containers

questions.question: Why does my app behind a TLS proxy not know the original request used HTTPS?

expected.evidence: by default, it wouldn't trust those headers

questions.question: How do I make the app server trust the X-Forwarded headers sent by a proxy?

expected.evidence: --forwarded-allow-ips

questions.question: How do I pin the FastAPI version so upgrades do not break my app?

expected.evidence: that would mean that you would use the versions 0.112.0 or above, but less than 0.113.0

questions.question: Which part of a FastAPI version number can introduce breaking changes?

expected.evidence: Breaking changes and new features are added in "MINOR" versions.

questions.question: Are new Pydantic versions compatible with FastAPI?

expected.evidence: new versions of Pydantic (above 1.0.0) are always compatible with FastAPI

questions.question: How do I start several worker processes for my FastAPI app?

expected.evidence: You can start multiple workers with the --workers command line option

questions.question: Does using multiple workers solve all the deployment concerns?

expected.evidence: using workers would mainly help with the replication part, and a little bit with the restarts, but you still need to take care of the others

questions.question: Which ASGI server does the fastapi command use by default?

expected.evidence: this is the one that comes by default in the fastapi command

questions.question: Which ASGI servers can I use besides Uvicorn?

expected.evidence: an ASGI server compatible with HTTP/2 and Trio among other features

questions.question: What command do I use to serve my FastAPI app in production?

expected.evidence: use fastapi run to serve your FastAPI application

questions.question: Why is a field with a default value marked as required in the response schema of the docs?

expected.evidence: The way to describe this in OpenAPI, is to mark that field as required, because it will always be there.

questions.question: Why does OpenAPI show two schemas, Item-Input and Item-Output, for the same model?

expected.evidence: you will see that there are two, one Item-Input and one Item-Output

questions.question: How do I disable syntax highlighting in Swagger UI?

expected.evidence: you can disable it by setting syntaxHighlight to False

questions.question: Can I pass JavaScript functions to Swagger UI through swagger_ui_parameters?

expected.evidence: These are JavaScript objects, not strings, so you can't pass them from Python code directly.

questions.question: How do I turn off the OpenAPI docs in production using an environment variable?

expected.evidence: disable OpenAPI (including the UI docs) by setting the environment variable OPENAPI_URL to the empty string

questions.question: Does hiding the API docs in production make my API secure?

expected.evidence: be the way to protect your API

questions.question: How do I disable the automatic docs before configuring a custom CDN?

expected.evidence: set their URLs to None when creating your FastAPI app

questions.question: When should I self-host the Swagger UI JavaScript and CSS files?

expected.evidence: need your app to keep working even while offline, without open Internet access, or in a local network

questions.question: Can I still use pydantic.v1 models in current FastAPI versions?

expected.evidence: using a pydantic.v1 model in your app will raise an error

questions.question: Is there a tool that automates migrating my code from Pydantic v1 to v2?

expected.evidence: This tool will help you to automatically change most of the code that needs to be changed.
